edit.description: the listing's dirent filter stops deciding readability — a record named like one reaches the read that refuses it
the listing's refusal, beside the read's own case in the unreachable-record block

summary: The listing's dirent filter drops the record the read refuses, so an unreadable record reads as no prior attempt on every surface a phase leg actually calls
acceptance: a record file the listing finds and cannot open refuses out of `readAll` as it already does out of `read`, so no surface a phase leg reaches — the selection map, a chain's `TickContext.priorAttempts`, `clearStale` — reads an unreadable record as no prior attempt and resets the repeated-failure count over it; a dirent that is not a record by name is still skipped in silence
tests: the prior-attempt listing refuses a record present and unreadable rather than omitting it
notes: Measured this tick: over a store holding one real record plus a directory at `<flumeDir>/prior-attempts/phase/plan.json`, `readAll` (`src/priorAttempts.ts:484`) answered `['phase:build']` while `read` (`:371`) refused the same ref — the `e.isFile()` test (`:498`) drops the dirent ahead of the read. `readAll` is what `src/waveTick.ts:107`, `src/singletonTick.ts:80` and `src/Dispatcher.ts:1214` call; `read` is reached from `src/tickAttempt.ts:252` alone.
